text.p: Portuguese construction group Sociedade de Construcao Soares da Costa is maintaining its forecast for revenues of 85 billion escudos by the end of 1997, director Antonio Frada said.

"The growth curve on sales volume in the first four months of 1997 confirms the forecast that at the end of the year Soares da Costa's (non-consolidated) sales will be 85 billion escudos, compared with a 1996 figure of just over 72 billion," said Frada. He declined to give figures for the first four months.

Frada said that Soares da Costa did not plan to sell off its real estate holdings in order to reduce the debt of the parent company. "We are not interested in selling our (real estate holdings) CIA and Mercados Novos," he told Reuters.
He said the debt levels of the two subsidiaries were unexceptional.
"Soares da Costa's liabilities will be cut by other measures, not by real estate sales, but rather by controlling costs and reining in some difficult outstanding loans," Frada said.
Soares da Costa's liabilities at the end of 1996 were 71 billion escudos.

Regarding reports that a consortium including Soares da Costa and ABB would lower its bid to build an urban transport system in Oporto by 10 billion escudos, Frada said that no decision had yet been taken.
In afternoon trade, Soares da Costa shares rose 23 escudos to 1,650 in volume of 4,930 shares on Lisbon bourse.
